results.title: Schur's inequality {\cite[Theorem~1]{hlp}}
results.statement: \label{lem:schur} For all real numbers $a, b, c \ge 0$, \[ a(a-b)(a-c) + b(b-a)(b-c) + c(c-a)(c-b) \ge 0 . \]

results.label: thm:amgm
results.statement: \label{thm:amgm} For all real numbers $a$ and $b$, \[ \frac{a + b}{2} \ge \sqrt{ab} . \]

change.printed: \label{thm:amgm} For all real numbers $a$ and $b$, \[ \frac{a + b}{2} \ge \sqrt{ab} . \]
change.corrected: For all real numbers $a, b \ge 0$, \[ \frac{a + b}{2} \ge \sqrt{ab} . \]
change.proof_change: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:sq} to $x = \sqrt{a}$ and $y = \sqrt{b}$, real numbers since $a, b \ge 0$: then $x^2 = a$, $y^2 = b$ and $xy = \sqrt{ab}$, so $a + b \ge 2\sqrt{ab}$.

findings.detail: False for negative numbers: for $a=b=-1$ the left side is $-1$ while the right side is $\sqrt{1}=1$. The proof takes $\sqrt{a}$ and $\sqrt{b}$, which are real numbers only when $a,b\ge 0$.
findings.suggested_repair: For all real numbers $a, b \ge 0$, \[ \frac{a + b}{2} \ge \sqrt{ab} . \]
